body:
Running `python scripts/extract_spa_strings.py --write` on 81933ac61 rewrites the AUTOGEN
block at -92/+35 msgids (net -57), so the checked-in anchor file no longer matches what the
extractor derives from the current SPA source.

Why it is not caught: tests/unit/test_spa_strings_anchored.py only asserts the one direction
that matters for correctness -- every SPA key IS anchored. Stale extras that no longer exist
in the SPA are harmless to users (they just add dead msgids for translators) so the suite
stays green while the file drifts.

Impact is translator-facing, not user-facing: dead msgids are offered for translation and
real ones churn. Worth a standalone regeneration PR with the diff actually reviewed --
notably whether any of the 92 removals are strings the extractor's scanner misses
(dynamically constructed keys) rather than genuinely dead ones.

Found while adding the v4.1.31 What's New entries (PR #1418), where a new label tripped the
anchoring test. Deliberately not bundled into that content PR at a release boundary.
title: cps/spa_strings.py AUTOGEN block has drifted ~57 msgids from the SPA source
